chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He who anthropomorphizes Allah with His creation is a polytheist. Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does not resemble anything, and nothing resembles Him. Everything that is imagined is other than Him.

The Compiler of this book (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The proof that Allah, the Glorified, does not resemble any of His creation in any dimension is that there is no dimension for any of His actions except that it is created (muhdathah), and no created dimension except that it indicates the creation of the One to whom it belongs. So if Allah, High be His Praise, resembled anything from His creation, it would indicate His creation in the same way it indicates the creation of the One to whom it belongs, because two things that are intellectually similar require one ruling due to their similarity. And the proof has been established that Allah, the Mighty and High, is Eternal (Qadim), and it is impossible for Him to be Eternal in one dimension and created in another. Another proof that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Eternal is that if He were created, it would be necessary that He has a Creator, because an action does not occur except through an agent, and the statement about His Creator would be like the statement about Him. And in this case, there is existence of a created being before a created being without a beginning, which is impossible. Hence, it is correct that there must be an Eternal Creator. And if that is so, then whatever necessitates the eternity of that Creator and indicates it, also necessitates the eternity of our Creator and indicates it.

key_terms.مَنْ شَبَّهَ اللَّهَ بِخَلْقِهِ: He who anthropomorphizes Allah with His creation
key_terms.مُشْرِكٌ: Polytheist / One who associates partners with God

ai.seo_question: What is the proof that Allah does not resemble His creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* rigorously defines divine transcendence (tanzih) by asserting that any entity comprehensible to the human mind (al-wahm) is inherently distinct from Allah. The compiler employs a rational argument regarding 'directions' (juhat) of action, demonstrating that since all directed actions are created, and Allah is eternal, He cannot possess created directions, thereby precluding any similarity to His creation. This establishes a foundational Shia theological principle that divine unity necessitates absolute uniqueness, free from the limitations of time, space, or form.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 36. Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari said on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Mohammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn `Umar that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

He who anthropomorphizes Allah with His Creation is an infidel. Verily, Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, does not resemble anything and nothing resembles Him. Everything that is imagined is other than Him.

The Compiler (may Allah have mercy on him) of this book says: The proof that nothing resembles Allah, the Glorified, in His Creation in any dimension, is that there is no dimension for any of His Actions except that it has a beginning [muhdathah]. Therefore, it Allah, High be His Praise, resembles anything from His Creation, then that would certainly give Him a beginning… At the same time, two things which are intellectually similar require one ruling due to their similarity. And the proof had been established for Allah, the Mighty and High, being without beginning [qadim], It is impossible that He may be Eternal in one dimension, and have beginning another. Another proof that Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is without beginning is that if He had a beginning then there must have been someone that gave Him a beginning, because an action requires an agent. And surely the word about one who gave beginning to Him is like the word about Him. And in this (case) there is existence of an eternal before an eternal that has no prior (to Him). This is impossible. Hence, it is correct that there must be an Eternal Creator. And if it is so, then whatever demands the eternity of that creator and indicates upon him, also demands the eternity of the Creator we believe in and indicates upon Him.
